issues.legal_issue: A former protected agricultural tenant does not retain tenancy rights merely by remaining in possession after a final order terminating the lease and the expiry of the protected-tenancy period, and the landlord's claim for mesne profits or, alternatively, rent does not by itself recognize or acquiesce in a continuing tenancy.
material_facts: The minor lessor obtained a final order under section 9A(2) of the Berar Regulation of Agricultural Leases Act terminating the lease and directing him to apply for possession after the specified date.
The tenant's protected status under the Berar Act expired, but he remained in possession.
The landlord sought mesne profits or, alternatively, lease amounts; the Court found that these claims did not recognize or acquiesce in a continuing tenancy.
The Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act contained no provision conferring tenancy rights on the tenant after his protected status had ended.
issues.conclusion: The lease was terminated by the final order, the tenant's protected status expired, and his continued possession did not give him continuing tenancy rights; the landlord's claims for mesne profits or rent did not amount to acquiescence in a tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9A(2) of the Berar Regulation of Agricultural Leases Act, the final order terminated the lease; after the protected status conferred by the Berar Act expired, the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act did not confer a further tenancy right on the occupant. A claim for mesne profits or, alternatively, rent did not establish recognition or acquiescence in a tenancy. The Court referred to sections 6, 36, 38 and 100(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, but cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: agricultural_tenancy_possession_dispute and final_lease_termination_order and protected_tenancy_status_expired and landlord_did_not_recognize_continuing_tenancy

predicates.agricultural_tenancy_possession_dispute: The parties disputed possession of agricultural land on the basis of an asserted tenancy.
predicates.final_lease_termination_order: An authority made a final order terminating the lease.
predicates.protected_tenancy_status_expired: The occupant's protected-tenancy status came to an end.
predicates.landlord_did_not_recognize_continuing_te: The landlord did not recognize a continuing tenancy, and claims for mesne profits or alternatively rent were not treated as such recognition.
predicates.former_lessee_has_no_continuing_tenancy_: The former lessee has no continuing tenancy right merely because the former lessee remains in possession.

issues.definition: When an agricultural possession dispute follows a final lease-termination order and the occupant's protected status has expired, the former lessee has no continuing tenancy right if the landlord did not recognize a continuing tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: An application for possession is not time-barred when it is filed within the applicable transitional period after the new tenancy regime comes into force.
material_facts: The landlord applied for possession on 11 January 1960.
The Court found that the application was filed within two years from the date the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act came into force.
issues.conclusion: The application for possession was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the application was filed within the applicable two-year period measured from the commencement of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.application_for_possession_in_transition: A party sought possession in a proceeding arising during the transition to a new tenancy regime.
predicates.application_filed_within_transition_wind: The party filed the application within the applicable transitional filing window.
predicates.application_is_not_time_barred: The application is not barred by limitation.

issues.definition: An application for possession in a transitional tenancy proceeding is not time-barred when it was filed within the applicable transitional filing window.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court is justified in supervisory review when a tribunal overturns a finding that a tenant's rights ended under a final termination order and the expiry of protected status.
material_facts: The appellate authority found that the final order had terminated the tenancy and that the occupant thereafter held possession other than as a tenant.
The Revenue Tribunal reversed that finding, treating the occupant as a protected lessee entitled to continuing status.
The High Court, exercising its powers under Article 227 of the Constitution, quashed the Tribunal's order and restored the order allowing the landlord's claim for possession.
issues.conclusion: The Revenue Tribunal was in error, and the High Court was justified in interfering with its order under Article 227.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 of the Constitution empowered the High Court to interfere with the Tribunal's order in the circumstances of this case because the Tribunal wrongly set aside the finding that the tenancy had ended. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: supervisory_review_of_tenancy_tribunal_order and tribunal_reversed_termination_finding and final_termination_order and protected_tenancy_status_expired

predicates.supervisory_review_of_tenancy_tribunal_o: A High Court reviewed a tenancy tribunal's order in supervisory proceedings.
predicates.tribunal_reversed_termination_finding: The tribunal overturned a finding that the occupant's tenancy had ended.
predicates.final_termination_order: An authority had made a final order terminating the lease.
predicates.protected_tenancy_status_expired: The occupant's protected-tenancy status had come to an end.
predicates.high_court_supervisory_interference_is_j: The High Court's supervisory interference with the tribunal's order is justified.

issues.definition: In supervisory review of a tenancy tribunal order, interference is justified when the tribunal reverses a termination finding despite a final termination order and the expiry of protected-tenancy status.
